thread:
maya: Quick design proposal — sample-weighted cost breakdown for the console. Problem: we sample invocation telemetry to control ingest. Naive multiply-by-1/sample_rate inflates variance for low-volume tenants and makes cache-savings attribution noisy. Proposal: publish an "estimated unit cost" with a confidence band and a shrinkage-adjusted estimator for low-n tenants. Also suggest how to allocate cache savings: ownership heuristic (route who created the prefix) + prorate for shared prefixes. Want quick reactions before I wire to the proto UI.

sam: quick q — dividing by sample_rate seems inevitable. How do you avoid noise for tiny tenants? will users freak out at big swings? :thinking:

dinesh: agree on variance issue. suggestion: use empirical Bayes shrinkage toward global mean. e.g.
```
adj_cost = (n/(n+alpha))*tenant_est + (alpha/(n+alpha))*global_mean
confidence = z * sqrt( var_obs / n ) / sample_rate
```
where n is sampled_invocations. choose alpha ~ 50 or based on previous epoch.

julie: UX note: label anything using this as "estimated" and show a small confidence sparkline tooltip. customers will want to see sample_rate and sample_window. also we should surface when we switched sampling configs.

kai: two more things:
- show an "effective unit cost" (cost/token after cache credits) per model sku and per-route
- expose cache-credit provenance: which route/machine earned the prefetch entry so ops can dispute allocation

ops-bot: sampler-service: deployed v2.1 -> default sample_rate=0.02 for low-cardinality routes. CI job: #deploy-218

maya: thanks — re: cache-credit provenance, my thought is to attach a short lineage (route id + tenant id + TTL) to cache entries and record a fingerprint on hit. For UI we show "likely owner" and a confidence score rather than absolute owner. For the shrinkage alpha we can make alpha configurable per-tenant-class.

sam: another edge: multi-model chains. attribution model? first/last token? or split by per-model CPU/time? users chain models a lot and expect fair split.

maya: propose proportional split by model inference cost (estimated tokens * model_unit_cost) for the chain. We'll compute chain_cost = sum(per-model_est_cost) then attribute proportionally. If sampling drops a model in the chain, mark chain as partial and show warn icon.

julie: for billing/legal: we must not use estimated numbers as invoices. show estimated in console but always compute billing from raw logs for invoicing window or switch to full-sample for billing period. flag that in the UI.

dinesh: ops idea: automatic switch to higher sample_rate or full-logging for tenants whose estimated monthly spend > X or when confidence < threshold. Then re-run attribution offline if needed.

maya: plan: I'll prototype an API patch returning {estimate, sample_rate, confidence_interval, attribution_breakdown, provenance_links}. Will open a proto PR and a small dashboard mock. If no objections I'll add alpha tuning and the autoswitch rules. cc @sam @dinesh for review.

sam: +1. can you add a small example response in the PR so frontend can mock EXACT payload? that speeds iteration.

julie: +1 from UX. add tooltip text copy for legal/billing disclaimers.

dinesh: +1 from infra. put the autoswitch as a separate toggle so we can experiment.

maya: great — will follow up with PR and mock screenshots tomorrow. :rocket:
